findings.observation: Both texts preserve 0 and 300000 and call them historical approximations, but only say they are not precise present-day conclusions. Neither says the old massless belief was experimentally disproved. This can leave a learner believing exact zero mass is merely an imprecise but still valid modern approximation.
findings.evidence: The bound Fermilab mass text explicitly says type-changing experiments disproved the historic massless belief. This is stronger than uncertainty about an exact mass value.
findings.action: Keep both existing numerical/math expressions untouched. Add a qualitative sentence in this existing block saying neutrino oscillation experiments disproved the old massless assumption and that the absolute masses remain under study. Do not claim every mass eigenstate is proven to have strictly nonzero mass, add an exact mass value, or retain light-speed necessity as a current fact.
findings.suggested_zh_sentence: 后来的中微子振荡实验否定了中微子全都没有静止质量的旧假设；其绝对质量仍在研究中。
findings.suggested_en_sentence: Later neutrino-oscillation experiments disproved the old assumption that neutrinos are massless; their absolute masses remain under study.
findings.dependent_anchor: /section_breaks/1/before may need affected-only rederivation if the final paragraph changes.

findings.observation: The historical elementary-neutron statement is rightly qualified, but the modern text stops at saying the old description must not be taken to imply no internal structure. It never supplies the established correction: the neutron is composite. The section therefore ends with avoidable ambiguity about its central example.
findings.evidence: The independently read Fermilab beta-decay page explicitly classifies protons/neutrons as composite and identifies their quark constituents.
findings.action: State qualitatively in the existing concluding block that neutrons are now known to be composite particles made of quarks. Keep the existing lesson that instability or stability alone does not decide whether a particle has constituents; preserve the deuterium nucleus example. Do not add quark counts or change source expressions.
findings.suggested_zh_sentence: 现在已知中子是由夸克组成的复合粒子。
findings.suggested_en_sentence: The neutron is now known to be a composite particle made of quarks.

findings.observation: The texts retain recognizable Pauli, Fermi and United States identities, but historical_entities declares only Switzerland. Pauli is undeclared in entries 2 and 3; Fermi in entry 4 and United States in entry 11 are also undeclared.
findings.evidence: The lesson skill requires per-block source-bound declarations of actual historical people and places, not merely correct visible translations.
findings.action: Add zh declarations for 泡利 at entries 2/3, 费米 at entry 4 and 美国 at entry 11, with reasons bound to p0382#3, p0382#4, p0382#5 and p0383#7 respectively. Add the corresponding English term/source_term mappings Pauli/泡利, Fermi/费米 and United States/美国; preserve translation in changes. Keep the existing Switzerland declaration. Do not reintroduce a scientifically misleading Pauli zero-mass attribution merely to repeat his name.

findings.observation: English word/number and word/math boundaries are missing. Literal phrases such as as16, About26 and in1956 are malformed even without a display test; the math-adjacent phrases likewise need ordinary English spacing.
findings.action: Insert spaces outside the unchanged math delimiters and around unchanged digits: as 16, About 26, in 1956, describes 200, about 300, at $300000$, nuclear $\beta$, symbol $\nu$, point $A$, producing 2 $\gamma$, and analogous listed cases. Do not change symbols, numbers, units, source_text or raw inputs.
